question.text: Let $a>b>0$ and $f(n)=a^{1 / n}-b^{1 / n}$,$J(n)=(a-b)^{1 / n}$ for all $n \geq 2,$ Then

solution.text:
Let $a=4, b=1$ and $n=2$
$\begin{array}{l}
\therefore \quad I(n)=a^{1 / n}-b^{1 / n} \\
=4^{1 / 2}-1^{1 / 2}=2-1=1 \\
\text { and } J(n)=(a-b)^{1 / n} \\
=(4-1)^{1 / 2}=\sqrt{3} \\
\therefore \quad J(n)>I(n)
\end{array}$
Similarly, we can prove for other values of $a, b, n$
